properties.name: MEASURED 2026-10-02 (0.77.0), limitation 3 CONFIRMED with its exact path. A held design refuses every `--call` write. --shared beside --call is ignored. The refusal says "stop that server" without naming --stop-shared or the server's URL. And `--remote <url> --call X` silently runs a stdio proxy instead, exit 0, nothing called
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), triage agent A, on limitation 3 of art:vscode-call-door-field-report-2026-10-02 ("One writer, and --call cannot join a shared server … call_one_tool opens the store directly"). Two scratch processes, isolated HOME.

① OBSERVED:
- A `--serve-shared --idle-timeout 15` server started on a scratch store and published `<g1>.server.json` (url http://127.0.0.1:43227/, pid).
- `--call get_node` and `--call graph_report` → exit 0 with the SNAPSHOT warning, correct content.
- `--call add_requirement …` → exit 1: "`add_requirement` writes, so it needs the graph itself and not a snapshot copy … another process already has the design graph … open. The graph is single-writer … Stop that server (or close the editor session using it) and run this again." Nothing written (get_node of that id after release: absent).
- The same write with `--shared --call` → identical refusal; --shared changes nothing.
- `--remote http://127.0.0.1:43227/ --call get_node …` and the same with a write → exit 0, EMPTY stdout, empty stderr at RUST_LOG=error. RUST_LOG=info shows only "working against a remote reflow2 server": the --remote branch (main.rs ~1106) returns before --call is read, so the call is dropped and a stdio proxy ran on /dev/null and exited.
- `--stop-shared` → "asked the shared server (pid …) to stop", and the rendezvous was removed.
Log: /home/ajs7/.claude/jobs/fa666a94/tmp/triage-A/measure.log (L3-*).

② PRECEDENT: the 2026-10-01 field fact (limitation 3, same observation); this decision's option (a).
③/④ CANDIDATES: (a) a deliberate choice in the door (a build should not write into a live session); (b) no route exists, because the in-process pipe cannot reach a remote holder; (c) the route exists (rendezvous plus proxy::run, which --shared uses) and the door never consults it.
(c) holds and (b) is refuted: the --shared client path finds the holder through reflow2_mcp::shared::ensure_server_async and forwards with proxy::run. (a) is true as well. The capability's text records the refusal as designed ("a writer refuses with the lock explanation"), and this decision's counter-argument records it as loud on purpose. So L3 is a scope decision, not a slip. The reporter's mechanism is exact.

WHAT THIS ADDS TO THE OPEN QUESTION (idea 2 of the report, option (a) here):
- The holder's address is already on disk beside the store, so option (a) needs no discovery.
- But `ensure_server_async` STARTS a daemon when none runs. Reused as-is, a one-shot call would leave a server holding the lock for 120 idle minutes. A door version should attach only, never spawn.
- The daemon is started with the client's --export-to, so a call routed through a daemon started that way gets the write-through. That is consistent with dec:idea-a-writing-call-exports-afterwards's interaction note.
- Today's refusal could cheaply name the way out: the server's URL from the rendezvous and `--stop-shared`. It names neither.
- `--remote URL --call X` is the natural thing to try for a held or pointer design, and it fails silently (exit 0, nothing done). It is the same class as fact:root-cause-one-shot-modes-return-before-the-pointer-check-and-opening-a-store-creates-it-2026-10-02: which flags count depends on which early return is taken, and clap declares no conflict between --call and --remote, --shared, --export-to or --only-if-present.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a Claude Code `--shared` session plus a VS Code door on the same design is a setup anyone runs today. The plan's note says that under Copilot alone no daemon holds the design.
